title: HF private storage limit reached for bentzbk: jta-market-lake (incl. MANIFEST.json) returns 403 to runners; ml.datasets.lake consumers blocked or falling back
note:
MEASURED 2026-11-05 11:48Z by lane ML-DATA-WIRING (session_01AFoLuNLZwgzom32C3hBXFE): the lake-parity run on #23287 (job 127222923139, head c0b111029) got HTTP 403 from huggingface.co/datasets/bentzbk/jta-market-lake/resolve/main/MANIFEST.json, body 'Private repository storage limit reached for bentzbk, please upgrade your plan ... or free up space'. HF_TOKEN present and the request reaches HF. Manager read 11:5xZ via HF MCP: the account bentzbk has 3 private repos (model woof_trade_organziation 2025-07-04, space wto 2025-07-07, dataset jta-market-lake last modified 2026-11-05) plus 2 public (ict-signals-dataset, space ict-training-job); the per-repo storage sizes were NOT readable from the tools. NOT established: whether the daily market-data-lake refresh is failing for the same cause. Blocked on: operator act (upgrade the HF plan, or free private storage, e.g. delete the two 2025 private repos if unused). Then: lane ML-DATA-WIRING re-runs parity; a health read of the daily lake refresh run follows. [2026-11-05 ~13:1xZ, Manager Session 2026-11-05b]
OPERATOR proposed more free accounts. Checked against the providers' own pages:
- KAGGLE forbids it. Terms of Use, read via rendered page: "You also may not have, control, or operate under more than one active Kaggle account or Kaggle User ID ... we may take action without notice, including banning your user account".
- HF terms do not name multiple accounts, but they ban "bypass restrictions", abuse of services and "Hosting excessive or irrelevant data", and allow suspension "with or without cause".
HF storage table: free user or org 100GB private; PRO $9/mo 1TB private.
Measured: MANIFEST.json is 33.6 MB (LFS), rewritten each refresh.
OPERATOR DECISION, popup verbatim: "Squash first, then free org".
PLAN:
(1) Lane HF-LAKE-SQUASH measures current versus history storage, super-squashes jta-market-lake, and adds a retention rule.
(2) If the account is still near the cap, the operator creates a free HF organization they own; the lane moves the lake there and repoints the loaders and HF_TOKEN use. This needs an operator act, which goes on the console asks panel. Moved surge->throttle by operator popup 2026-11-05 ~18:30Z (surge plan triage; cap ~60-65% weekly). 2026-11-05 lane HF-LAKE-SQUASH: MEASURED on a runner (PR #23333 job 127283415795): lake current revision 100.34 GB vs total used 100.31 GB, history overhead ~0 (-31.7 MB), so the squash was NOT run (would free ~0, irreversible). Retention is measure+alert only. Free-storage options + recommendation: docs/research/hf-lake-free-storage-options-2026-11-05.md. Trainer VM disk 100 GB, 85 GB used (issue #23351). 2026-11-05 ~14:51Z OPERATOR DECISION (popup, verbatim): "Kaggle 1 GB pilot first (Rec.)". Lane HF-LAKE-SQUASH runs the pilot via .github/workflows/hf-lake-kaggle-pilot.yml (PR #23333): ~1 GB frozen crypto 1m shards -> private Kaggle dataset metis-market-lake on the EXISTING account; measures file limits, version-vs-quota, read path/speed, ToS; deletes nothing from HF; moving the frozen history needs one more operator OK. 2026-11-05 ~16:40Z lane HF-LAKE-SQUASH PILOT RESULT (PR #23333 runs 42055574691, 42060325476; table in docs/research/hf-lake-free-storage-options-2026-11-05.md): 867 MB / 90 frozen crypto 1m partitions (6 symbols) -> private Kaggle dataset metis-market-lake on the existing account. HF READ was refused at the cap so the stage rebuilt from Binance Vision. Upload 102 s; runner download 62-72 MB/s byte-exact; Kaggle CPU kernel reads 867 MB at 122 MB/s; 120 top-level files accepted (docs say 50); Kaggle auto-unpacks .tar shards into folders; quota-vs-versions NOT readable by API (needs the Account-tab number). Go: technical GO in steps; needs (1) Account-tab number, (2) 10 GB/5k-file step, (3) operator OK to free HF after copy. Nothing deleted from HF. 2026-11-05 ~16:59Z OPERATOR APPROVED (popup, verbatim): "10 GB trial (Rec.)" for the Kaggle step: ~10 GB of cold lake data into a private dataset on the same account, read-back + checksum verification; no deletion anywhere, no new accounts, nothing in the Models space. OPERATOR ACCOUNT-TAB READING at that moment: Private Datasets 2.89 GB of 214.75 GB; Private Models 0 B of 214.75 GB. LANE READING of that number: by then metis-market-lake had 6 versions in 3 distinct contents of 0.867 GB (identical re-uploads within a run), plus ~0.17 GB of other datasets' current versions: current-version-only would read ~1.0 GB, 'old versions count, deduplicated by content' would read ~2.8 GB; 2.89 GB fits the second. Not conclusive (the 4 older datasets have 23/2/138/15 versions); design assumes old versions COUNT: upload the cold set once, never re-version it. 2026-11-05 ~17:00Z operator (chat): "We can also try hosting private models there if it opens more storage/compute"; ~17:02Z: "Ok, let's also keep backups on kaggle (on private)" -> row KAGGLE-BACKUPS. Kaggle Models pilot (copy not move; ml/served/*/model.json 3 files ~16 MB + registry-store 19 MB/106 files on the trainer) follows the 10 GB dataset trial. 2026-11-05 ~18:38Z 10 GB TRIAL RESULT (run 42071813032 build+upload; read-backs run 42083376048 on 1fd337715): private dataset metis-market-lake now holds 77 tar shards = 2,396 frozen crypto 1m partitions, 300 symbols, 10,013,076,431 B, built from data.binance.vision (HF reads refused at the cap) in 31 min; upload+register <3 min. READ-BACK on the NEW version (first attempt wrongly verified the old 4-shard version because 'datasets status' says ready before the new version registers; now the checks poll the served MANIFEST note and fail on <50 shards): GitHub runner via Kaggle API 10,013,092,757 B in 120 s (83 MB/s) after the download archive became available (404 until then, ~45 min after upload); Kaggle CPU kernel (internet off) full read 195.7 s (51 MB/s), ~5 min push-to-complete. CHECKSUM LEVEL: file count + exact bytes per shard only (this upload predates per-member SHA-256; Kaggle unpacks tars so shard hashes cannot be re-checked); manifests written from now on carry a SHA-256 per member and the verifier checks them. Top-level entries 79 (docs say max 50; accepted). Operator quota to re-read on the Account tab: Datasets was 2.89 GB of 214.75 GB before this upload. 2026-11-05 ~18:40Z OPERATOR APPROVED (popup, verbatim): "Go, full copy (Rec.)" -> copy the FULL frozen crypto history (~75-90 GB) to private Kaggle dataset(s) on the existing account, with per-member SHA-256 manifests and verification.
